newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: TENNIS-CHANG CRUSHES FRANA IN SINGAPORE OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG CRUSHES FRANA IN SINGAPORE OPEN.

text.p: World number two Michael Chang routed Javier Frana of Argentina 6-4 6-1 to reach the semifinals of the men's Singapore Open on Friday.
Frana had battled back from 5-2 down in the first set and was within two points of snatching the set when he committed two consecutive errors to allow Chang to escape.
Chang did not make any mistakes in the second set and broke Frana twice to wrap up the quarter-final match.
"You never want to be up 5-2 and end up losing the set," Chang told reporters. "It was very crucial for me to win the last game in the first set."
Sweden's Thomas Johansson reached the semifinals at the expense of second seed and Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek after the Dutchman failed to start the third set and retired with a knee injury.
They split the first two sets, Krajicek winning the opener 7-5 and then losing the second, 7-3 in a tiebreak.
In the other quarter-finals, unseeded Greg Rusedski of Britain fired 16 aces past Russian Andrei Olhovskiy to win 7-6 6-2 and set up a semifinal match with Chang on Saturday.
In a battle of qualifiers, American Jonathan Stark won two tight tiebreakers to emerge a 7-6 7-6 victor over Germany's Martin Sinner. He will meet Johansson in the other semifinal.
